newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sets Q4 wage indexation at 6.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Romania sets Q4 wage indexation at 6.0 percent.

text.p: Romania's government, facing elections in November and threats of labour unrest, has offered 6.0 percent wage indexation for the fourth quarter of 1996 to counter the impact of price rises expected in the cold season.
Finance Minister Florin Georgescu said the indexation level would cover 81.2 percent of 12-month inflation estimated at around 30 percent in December 1996.
"The cabinet decided to give 6.0 percent wage indexation after last week's negotiations with trade unions," Georgescu told a news conference after Wednesday's cabinet meeting.
The last such move was in July, when the government set state-sector wage indexation at 6.0 percent for the second and third quarters of the year to compensate for energy, fuel and bread price hikes.
Trade unions want 10 percent indexation of gross monthly wages in the state sector, saying this would prevent a further drop in living standards.
The two biggest labour unions, BNS and Cartel Alfa, have called protest rallies in Bucharest and several big towns on Thursday to press their wage indexation demands.
Georgescu repeated the government's pledge to stick to the year-end inflation target of 30 percent.

Local economic analysts say a forecast of 45 percent annual inflation would be more realistic, as the ruling Socialists, seeking re-election in November, may be tempted to give in to labour demands for higher wages.

Monthly inflation was 3.8 percent in August, when year-on-year inflation was 44.2 percent. The August average gross monthly wage was 456,841 lei. ($=3,245 lei) -- Diana Voicu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
